## WebQuiz 2.0.1

WebQuiz 2.0 is a full rewrite of the program in Go. It is **one file with no other parts to install**: no Python, no pip. Your quizzes, your `webquiz.yaml`, your CSV files and your folders work as before. The HTTP API, the config keys and the quiz format are the same as in 1.19.

2.0.1 is the first update after the 2.0 test build. If you tried the 2.0 test build, read the next part. If you come from 1.19, the whole page is for you.

### New since the 2.0 test build

- **Desktop version with a tray icon.** On a teacher's computer, WebQuiz now runs as an icon in the system tray (on macOS, in the menu bar), with no console window. Its menu shows the address that students open, and it opens the admin panel, live stats and the file manager. **Quit** writes the answers that are not saved yet, then stops WebQuiz. The Windows installer now installs this version. For macOS there is `WebQuiz.app`, one app for Apple Silicon and Intel. The console version stays for servers and the Raspberry Pi. More below, under "Desktop version with a tray icon".
- **The quiz page says whether an answer is right.** While correct answers are shown, the page shows **"✓ Правильно"** or **"✗ Неправильно"** next to the **"Продовжити"** button (in English: "✓ Correct" or "✗ Incorrect").
- **Faster start of a lesson on slow Wi-Fi.** The scripts and styles of the pages are sent gzip-compressed, about 70% smaller.
- **Phone layout as in 1.19.** Picture options are as wide as the phone screen again. The theme button and the student's name now scroll away with the page. In the 2.0 test build they stayed on the screen and covered the text under them.
- **Config form fix.** In the 2.0 test build, saving the config form in the file manager could write a broken `webquiz.yaml`, for example when `registration` was the last section of the file and the language changed in the same save. The save failed, and the change was lost. Now the form writes a correct file. As an extra guard, WebQuiz checks the new file before it saves it: if the file would change anything that the form did not ask for, the save is refused with a clear message, and the old file stays.

### Downloads

WebQuiz comes in two versions of the same program. Take the **desktop version** for a teacher's computer: it shows an icon in the system tray. Take the **console version** for a server, a Raspberry Pi without a screen or the command line.

- **Desktop version**:
  - **Windows** (10 or newer): `webquiz-windows-setup.exe` (installer).
  - **macOS** (12 or newer): `webquiz-macos-app.zip` (`WebQuiz.app`, one app for Apple Silicon and Intel).
  - **Linux**: `webquiz-linux-desktop.zip` (64-bit PC, a desktop with a system tray).
- **Console version**:
  - **Windows** (10 or newer): `webquiz-windows.exe.zip` (portable).
  - **macOS** (12 or newer): `webquiz-macos-apple-silicon.zip` (M1 and newer) or `webquiz-macos-intel.zip`.
  - **Linux**: `webquiz-linux.zip` (64-bit PC), `webquiz-linux-arm64.zip` (Raspberry Pi 3, 4, 5 with a 64-bit system), `webquiz-linux-arm.zip` (older Raspberry Pi boards: Zero, 1, 2).
- **Documentation** as PDF: `webquiz-documentation-en.pdf` and `webquiz-documentation-uk.pdf`.

The `pip install webquiz` package is not published for 2.0. The old Python version stays at [oduvan/webquiz](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz).

### What is different from 1.19

**Desktop version with a tray icon** (new)
- WebQuiz runs as an icon in the system tray (on macOS, in the menu bar). There is no console window to keep open or to close by mistake.
- The menu shows the version and the address that students open, for example `WebQuiz 2.0.1 — http://192.168.1.5:8080/`. It opens the admin panel, live stats and the file manager in the browser. **Quit** stops WebQuiz and first writes the answers that are not saved yet, as Ctrl+C does.
- When WebQuiz cannot start, the first line of the menu says why. A busy port gets a plain message: "port 8080 is used by another program. Maybe WebQuiz is already running". The error is also in the log file, and Windows shows it in a message box.
- The menu is in Ukrainian, or in English with `language: en`.
- **Windows**: the installer now installs the desktop version, with a Start menu shortcut. The portable zip stays the console version.
- **macOS**: `WebQuiz.app` works on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Put it into a folder of its own, for example `Documents/WebQuiz`: the data is kept next to it. The app is not signed by Apple, so open it the first time with right-click > **Open**. When the app is in the Applications folder, or macOS runs it from a read-only copy, the data goes to `Documents/WebQuiz`, and the menu shows that folder.
- **Linux**: `webquiz-linux-desktop` needs a desktop with a system tray: KDE, XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE or Ubuntu. Plain GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension.
- The console version works as before.

**Install and start**
- One binary per platform. Files live next to the program, as in the 1.19 binaries. Set `WEBQUIZ_BINARY_DIR` to use another folder. This is useful for a service, for example on a Raspberry Pi data partition.
- The browser opens the admin page when the program starts, as in the 1.19 binary.
- Minimum systems: macOS 12 and Windows 10.
- `webquiz --version` now prints the real version. 1.19 always printed `1.0.0`.
- `webquiz -d` on Windows now says that it is not supported. 1.19 crashed there.
- The "new version" message in the admin panel now looks at the releases of [oduvan/webquiz-go](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go). 1.19 looked at PyPI.

**New look**
- All pages are rebuilt with React and Tailwind: the quiz, the admin panel, the file manager, live stats and the CSV table. They have the same features. The phone layout works as before (768 px wide and less).
- The scripts and styles of the pages are sent gzip-compressed, about 70% smaller. 1.19 sent its pages uncompressed. This helps on slow Wi-Fi, for example with a Raspberry Pi Zero.
- After an answer, while correct answers are shown, the quiz page now says **"✓ Правильно"** or **"✗ Неправильно"** next to the **"Продовжити"** button (in English: "✓ Correct" or "✗ Incorrect"). 1.19 showed only colors and labels, so a partly right answer to a several-answers question looked right, though it counted as wrong.

**Checker code of text questions**
- Checkers now run in Starlark, a small Python-like language. Normal Python checkers keep working. This includes `assert` with a message, f-strings with formats, `**`, chained comparisons like `0 < x < 10`, `math`, `to_int`, `distance`, `direction_angle`, string methods, loops and your own functions.
- These do not work: `try` / `except`, `raise`, `class`, `import`, `with`, `global`, `bytes()` and `fail()`.
- `len()` and indexing of text count bytes, not letters. For Ukrainian text, use `len(list(user_answer))` and `list(user_answer)[0]`.
- A checker now stops after 2 seconds or when it uses too much memory, and the answer counts as wrong. In 1.19 a checker like `while True: pass` could hang the server.
- When a quiz loads, the log gets a warning for each checker that the new version cannot run. Check your text questions once after you update.

**Bugs of 1.19 that are fixed**
- `/admin`, `/files` and `/live-stats` without the last slash now open the page. 1.19 showed 404, so the link printed at start did not work.
- If switching to a quiz file fails, the running quiz stays. 1.19 cleared the students first.
- Answers that waited for the 5-second CSV write are now written when you switch quizzes and when the server stops. 1.19 lost them.
- Quiz names with a folder part are refused. 1.19 let a name like `..%2F` reach files outside `quizzes/`.
- Downloading a quiz archive with an empty folder no longer copies the `.zip` file into `quizzes/`.
- Saving the running quiz in the file manager restarts it, as the docs always said.
- Live stats show the total points of the new quiz right after a switch. 1.19 kept the old total until a reload.
- The tunnel config download from an IPv6 tunnel server works.
- A config value of the wrong type now works. For example, `master_key: 12345` or `port: "8080"` are read as the text or number you meant. In 1.19 a numeric master key made the admin login fail.
- Saving a quiz in the admin editor keeps the keys that the editor does not show, such as the quiz `description` and keys it does not know. 1.19 lost them on every save.
- The old admin page had 11 small bugs. The new page does not copy them. One example: "Save and continue" on `x.yaml` made `x.yaml.yaml`.

**Kept as in 1.19**
- The file manager page shows the whole `webquiz.yaml`, including `admin.master_key` and any `auth_header_token`, to every computer on the local network that opens `/files/`. Keep your network private.

### Docs

The user guide for [English](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go/tree/master/docs/en) and [Ukrainian](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go/tree/master/docs/uk) is updated, with new screenshots. It is also online at <https://oduvan.github.io/webquiz-go/>.
